data.name: OpenAI Finds Smarter AI Models Harder to Monitor

data.name: AI Shifts Software Interviews from LeetCode to Real-World Challenges
data.summary: Software engineering interviews are moving away from disliked LeetCode problems toward sessions with large codebases, AI tools, and a focus on communication and judgment. Engineer Gergely Orosz notes this leaves hiring more subjective, requiring hands-on AI skills and clear explanations during the process. A Reddit-shared Bloomberg experience highlighted the hurdles: a candidate tackled a Django-Python codebase with unclear AI guidelines, passed tests, but still got rejected. Data shows AI mentions in interviews surging fourfold, while some firms like Anthropic drop traditional coding challenges entirely.

data.name: WorkflowArena Benchmark Tests AI Team Management on Real Projects
data.summary: Einsia AI released WorkflowArena, a new benchmark with 145 tasks across eight professional fields like software engineering, finance, and 3D modeling. It challenges top AI models to orchestrate teams of agents on long projects, scoring both final deliverables and delegation decisions via hidden verifiers. Leading models like Claude Opus 5.5 completed just 36.95% of tasks fully, revealing gaps in workflow coordination. The open-source setup on GitHub lets researchers test their own systems and study how agents handle integration failures.

data.name: Lila Sciences Unveils Open-Ended AI Research Breakthroughs
data.summary: Lila Sciences released a vision blog and four preprints from its Open-Endedness team, led by Kenneth Stanley, challenging ideas like whether more data always improves AI or if rewarding creativity directly sparks the best results. Key work introduces UFOs, a technique for unified factored representations that create sharper, more stable networks, as shown in a skull image comparison where Picbreeder-style training beats blurry standard results. The papers also tackle the 'creative paradox' and training LLMs to stay naïve for fresh perspectives, with researchers praising the potential for better coding agents and tying into the company's AI Science Factories.

data.name: Debate Heats Over Democratic AI Regulation Plans
data.summary: Critics describe the ideas as a sweeping Democratic push after election gains, including a new Department of AI to license advanced models trained on massive compute power, mandatory kill switches, and strict ID checks for chatbots. Bipartisan efforts like the AI Kill Switch Act from Reps. Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran aim to let the Department of Homeland Security throttle powerful systems in emergencies. While some see these as vital safeguards against risks like deepfakes, others warn of stifled innovation, authoritarian overreach, and threats to free expression—no full laws have passed yet.
